name: dump_wrap
explanation: Tempester Voice 1.5.1.1: the dump stream wraps to PC 0 at the end of the implemented flash. [routine] ([address], the 0xF800 reply) reads the instruction at the 16-bit pointer [address] and adds 2: DSI's pointer runs on past PC [address], the last implemented instruction of the dsPIC33FJ64MC804 (stream byte 66,047), and a read there stopped the chip on the machine (14/11/2026: a second full backup of Main 1.6.6.0 / 1.6.7.0; on DSI 1.5 every byte then reads 0xFF and the voice is silent until power-off, on Tempester Voice 1.5.1.0 the trap resets the chip). Now the pointer goes back to 0 when it reaches 0xAC00, so no Main, however it reads (Tempester 1.6.6.0 / 1.6.7.0, the stock Debug menu « Send Voice OS » twice), can make this chip read unimplemented flash: the stream is the flash itself, period 66,048 bytes. The high word [address] is no longer carried into (it stays 0 from reset; the 0xF5nn handler of parser_guard.s still clears it). Cost: the 0xF800 reply is written a few cycles later than in 1.5.1.0, still before DSI's and before the Main's 0xFF00 read (the Voice simulator timing).

edits.why: goto [address] ; was "mov #[address],W6 ; mov [W6],W7" (the 32-bit increment, [address], now unreached)
mov #0xac00,W6 ; past the last implemented instruction (PC [address])
the low byte of the instruction, as [address]
